content:
miriam: Heads-up — I'm opening a PR to change the gpu-pool Terraform module to support a mixed preemptible+demand pool, weighted instance preferences, and the new interruption-handler Lambda. Want quick sync on rollout strategy and tagging.

tony: 👍 can you paste the module diff? curious about how we express weights in TF

miriam: gist of the change is adding a new `preemptible_mix` object and a `canary_percentage` var. weights are just a map of instance_type -> weight, used to build the capacity-weights in the autoscaling group.

miriam: snippet:
```hcl
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/internal-modules//gpu-pool?ref=v2"

  preemptible_mix = {
    enabled = true
    percent = 0.15
    instance_weights = {
      g5.2xlarge = 70
      g5.4xlarge = 30
    }
  }

  canary_percentage = var.canary_percentage
}
```

elaine: :eyes: what about AMI rotation? last time a bad AMI rolled out and caused kernel panics on preemptibles.

miriam: added an `ami_tag` policy: LPs must use `redwood-inference/gpu-ami:stable` tag. The module will look up latest image by that tag and set id in launch template. That allows safe rollouts independent of the TF change.

raj: interruption handling? we need the SQS + lambda path we tested last month

miriam: yes — the launch template user-data installs the interruption watcher that calls the new lambda with instance metadata. The lambda publishes to cluster-control SSM param and triggers cordon/drain via the k8s controller. User-data fragment:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
/usr/local/bin/interrupt-watcher --endpoint https://int-handler.redwood.internal --region ${aws_region} &
```

miriam: The TF change creates the watcher IAM role + the lambda + SQS queue. The lambda also tags instances with `evict:on` for observability so billing/ops can filter.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline: terraform plan for module/gpu-pool succeeded on feature branch miriam/preemptible-mix (build 4578)

tony: rollout plan idea: 1) canary 5% of pool capacity in us-west-2 only, 2) verify metrics for 48h, 3) bump to 20% and include eu-west-1, 4) full rollout.

elaine: also need node-level graceful drain timeout bump for GPUS to 15m (pods can checkpoint), and PDBs updated.

raj: agree. add a kill-signal delay in the k8s daemonset so node termination doesn't OOM pods prematurely.

miriam: I'll add terraform var `canary_percentage` (default 0) and a `regions` list for canary. Also add `ami_lifecycle = "tagged"` default.

ton y: how will we verify cost savings? we need pre/post per-token GPU-hours and preemptible evictions metric.

miriam: module will emit CloudWatch metrics for `PreemptibleEvictions`, `CanaryErrorRate` and push to our metrics pipeline. We'll run a quick delta query against the last 7 days baseline.

sre-oncall: one ops concern: mixed pools can cause capacity fragmentation. Add a fallback policy: when preemptible capacity < 10% of requested, route to ondemand/dedicated

miriam: yes, added routing policy to the smart router. Implementation: fallback_label in ASG lifecycle hooks and a k8s node affinity rule so critical workloads pin to dedicated nodes.

elaine: tagging needs: billing:env, billing:team, infra:pool, infra:preemptible=true|false. We also want `ami:stable` tag on AMI date.

raj: small nit: prefer `preemptible=true` rather than `preemptible:on` so it's boolean-like for Cost engine.

miriam: changed.

tony: CI/TF steps to roll canary:
- terraform apply -var canary_percentage=5 -var canary_regions=["us-west-2"]
- run smoke job `smoke/gpu-canary` (10 runs)
- monitor `PreemptibleEvictions` and `PodDrainLatency`

miriam: will open PR with docs + smoke job link. tagging + AMI policy in README.

elaine: :thumbsup: add a kill-switch variable `disable_preemptible` default false so we can revert quickly via TF if something goes sideways.

miriam: added `disable_preemptible`.

deploy-bot: PR 612 opened by miriam: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/612

tony: I'll review today. if LGTM I'll coordinate smoke runs with QA and schedule canary for Tue 02:00 UTC.

raj: do we need to update the incident runbook? Last time evictions spiked and SRE had to manually cordon.

sre-oncall: yes please — add a short runbook section: how to forcibly drain nodes, rollback var, and how to mute the lambda notifications if it's a noisy false positive.

miriam: will add runbook snippets and include a checklist in PR. thanks everyone.

elaine: one last ask — add a small extra metric for GPU-utilization-per-instance-type. helps to tune weights.

miriam: good call. adding `GPUUtilizationByType` metric emit in the watcher.

tony: :shipit: pending minor comments

miriam: merging after fixes, will post canary schedule here.
